model_note.S:
cc: Sudden arm weakness and difficulty speaking

HPI: 29 yo f. Patient reports: I was last completely well 45 minutes ago. My right arm and the right side of my face feel weak. There is no pain spreading anywhere. The arm feels heavy and difficult to lift. I dropped a mug and cannot write normally. It began suddenly and has not improved. It happened while eating breakfast; my husband saw the onset. Rest has not helped. There is no movement trigger. I have taken no treatment for it. I had no previous episode like this. My right arm suddenly became weak. I have trouble finding the right words.

Patient perspective: Will I be able to speak normally again?

PMH: Hypertension and type 2 diabetes diagnosed at age 19; no previous stroke.

PSH: No recent surgery or bleeding.

Meds: Metformin 500 mg twice daily and lisinopril 10 mg daily; no anticoagulant.

Allergies: No known drug allergies.

SH: Smokes 5 cigarettes daily for 8 years. Two alcoholic drinks weekly. No cocaine or other recreational drugs. Delivery coordinator; lives with husband who witnessed the onset.

FH: Mother had stroke at 70; father diabetes; brother hypertension.

ROS: Neurologic - Reports focal weakness. Reports speech change. Denies headache. Denies seizure. Cardiovascular - Denies palpitations. Denies chest pain. Denies syncope. General - Denies fever. Denies chills. Denies fatigue.
Reproductive history: I do not think I am pregnant, but I have not taken a pregnancy test.

model_note.O:
Vitals: T 98.5 F oral, P 86 bpm, BP 168/94 mmHg, R 18 rpm, Pulse Ox 98% on room air, Ht 5' 7", Wt 165 lbs

General: Alert but has difficulty finding words.

Heart: Regular rhythm without murmur.

Lungs: Clear breath sounds bilaterally.

Neuro: Right lower facial weakness with forehead movement preserved; speech effortful. Right arm strength 3/5, left arm 5/5; both legs 5/5. Reduced light touch in the right hand compared with the left. Alert, recognizes self and location; naming is impaired.

Osteopathic: C1 paraspinal tissue texture change with mild tenderness on the right.

Skin: No visible rash on the inspected arms.
P: 1. Activate EMS/stroke pathway immediately; establish exact last-known-well and witness contact, obtain point-of-care glucose and urgent brain/vascular imaging through the stroke team; keep oral intake withheld until swallow safety is assessed; explain time-sensitive treatment eligibility and do not delay transfer to complete an elective exam or note.

2. Check bedside glucose immediately and treat a confirmed low value through the emergency team; reassess neurologic deficits afterward without abandoning stroke evaluation if they persist; explain that metabolic mimics need rapid testing.

3. Obtain urgent brain imaging through the stroke pathway to assess structural causes; involve neurology if a mass is identified; explain that this lower-probability possibility cannot be confirmed by the history and must not delay emergency assessment.

cc: Sudden arm weakness and difficulty speaking

HPI: 29 yo f. Patient reports: I was last completely well 5 hours ago. My right arm and the right side of my face feel weak. There is no pain spreading anywhere. The arm feels heavy and difficult to lift. I dropped a mug and cannot write normally. It began suddenly and has not improved. It happened while eating breakfast; my husband saw the onset. Rest has not helped. There is no movement trigger. I have taken no treatment for it. I had no previous episode like this. My right arm suddenly became weak. I have trouble finding the right words.

Patient perspective: Will I be able to speak normally again?

PMH: Hypertension and type 2 diabetes diagnosed at age 19; no previous stroke.

PSH: No recent surgery or bleeding.

Meds: Metformin 500 mg twice daily and lisinopril 10 mg daily; no anticoagulant.

Allergies: No known drug allergies.

SH: Smokes 5 cigarettes daily for 8 years. Two alcoholic drinks weekly. No cocaine or other recreational drugs. Delivery coordinator; lives with husband who witnessed the onset.

FH: Mother had stroke at 70; father diabetes; brother hypertension.

ROS: Neurologic - Reports focal weakness. Reports speech change. Denies headache. Denies seizure. Cardiovascular - Denies palpitations. Denies chest pain. Denies syncope. General - Denies fever. Denies chills. Denies fatigue.
Reproductive history: I do not think I am pregnant, but I have not taken a pregnancy test.

Vitals: T 98.5 F oral, P 86 bpm, BP 168/94 mmHg, R 18 rpm, Pulse Ox 98% on room air, Ht 5' 7", Wt 165 lbs

General: Alert but has difficulty finding words.

Heart: Regular rhythm without murmur.

Lungs: Clear breath sounds bilaterally.

Neuro: Right lower facial weakness with forehead movement preserved; speech effortful. Right arm strength 3/5, left arm 5/5; both legs 5/5. Reduced light touch in the right hand compared with the left. Alert, recognizes self and location; naming is impaired.

Osteopathic: C1 paraspinal tissue texture change with mild tenderness on the right.

Skin: No visible rash on the inspected arms.
P: 1. Activate EMS/stroke pathway immediately; establish exact last-known-well and witness contact, obtain point-of-care glucose and urgent brain/vascular imaging through the stroke team; keep oral intake withheld until swallow safety is assessed; explain time-sensitive treatment eligibility and do not delay transfer to complete an elective exam or note.

2. Check bedside glucose immediately and treat a confirmed low value through the emergency team; reassess neurologic deficits afterward without abandoning stroke evaluation if they persist; explain that metabolic mimics need rapid testing.

3. Obtain urgent brain imaging through the stroke pathway to assess structural causes; involve neurology if a mass is identified; explain that this lower-probability possibility cannot be confirmed by the history and must not delay emergency assessment.

cc: Sudden arm weakness and difficulty speaking

HPI: 29 yo f. Patient reports: I was last completely well 45 minutes ago. My right arm and the right side of my face feel weak. There is no pain spreading anywhere. The arm feels heavy and difficult to lift. I dropped a mug and cannot write normally. It began suddenly and has not improved. It happened while eating breakfast; my husband saw the onset. Rest has not helped. There is no movement trigger. I have taken no treatment for it. I had no previous episode like this. My right arm suddenly became weak. I have trouble finding the right words.

Patient perspective: Will I be able to speak normally again?

Meds: Metformin 500 mg twice daily and lisinopril 10 mg daily; no anticoagulant.

Neuro: Right lower facial weakness with forehead movement preserved; speech effortful. Right arm strength 3/5, left arm 5/5; both legs 5/5. Reduced light touch in the right hand compared with the left. Alert, recognizes self and location; naming is impaired.

P: 1. Activate EMS/stroke pathway immediately; establish exact last-known-well and witness contact, obtain point-of-care glucose and urgent brain/vascular imaging through the stroke team; keep oral intake withheld until swallow safety is assessed; explain time-sensitive treatment eligibility and do not delay transfer to complete an elective exam or note. Use short sentences, allow extra response time, verify yes/no responses, and include the witness with the patient’s consent.

2. Check bedside glucose immediately and treat a confirmed low value through the emergency team; reassess neurologic deficits afterward without abandoning stroke evaluation if they persist; explain that metabolic mimics need rapid testing.

3. Obtain urgent brain imaging through the stroke pathway to assess structural causes; involve neurology if a mass is identified; explain that this lower-probability possibility cannot be confirmed by the history and must not delay emergency assessment.
